blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型代理商通过闭路行动政策运作,其决策空间由代理管来定义. 我们调查这个操作空间如何塑造计算机辅助设计(CAD)中的代理行为和政策学习,这个专业领域的特点是持续状态、几何限制和长视距程序。 我们在DeciCAD中即时分析这一视角,这是一种域-内在的利用,它暴露了语义上的CAD行动,以决策为导向的观察,环境反馈,以及持续的状态过渡. 在此基础上,我们开发了一个学习管道,从互动轨迹中提取因果决策监督,并通过监督微调(SFT)和几何定位在线强化学习(RL)来改进政策. 在四个CAD基准中,DeciCAD实现了最好的F1和相交结合(IoU),同时相对于一个通用编码管减少了45-88%的模型输出信号. 在相应的监督下,其SFT政策将F1从0.6883提高到了0.7437,并且超过了编码政策;随后的在线RL进一步将几何学可用率从66.5%提高到了73.5%,F1提高到了0.7880. 这些结果表明,利用手段带来的决策空间在物质上影响到CAD的代理执行和政策学习。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used as agents to operate
professional software and complete long-horizon
tasks ( Achiam et al. 2023 ; Naveed et al. 2025 ; Guo et al. 2024 ) .
Computer-aided design (CAD) is a particularly demanding setting for
such agents ( Willis et al. 2020 ; Wu et al. 2021 ) .
Unlike one-shot content generation, CAD modeling requires a sequence of
state-dependent operations over a persistent design document.
An agent must create and modify sketches, constraints, features, and geometric objects;
inspect intermediate results; recover from execution failures;
and maintain references across long interaction trajectories.
In this process, the model outputs are interpreted as actions:
each action changes the current CAD state, produces execution feedback, and conditions
the next decision ( Yao et al. 2023 ; Schick et al. 2023 ) .
The effectiveness of a CAD agent therefore depends not only on the underlying model
and its reasoning strategy,
but also on how CAD actions, states, and execution outcomes
are represented to the model.

Such a model–environment boundary is defined by an agent harness ( Yang et al. 2024 ) . In CAD, a harness determines which design operations the
model can express, which parts of the evolving design state it can inspect, and
how execution outcomes are returned for subsequent decisions.
A general-purpose coding harness may expose the CAD system through programs,
libraries, and runtime feedback, whereas a domain-native harness may expose
structured CAD actions and object-level observations.
Consequently, even when the model, task, and CAD backend remain fixed,
different harnesses can present the model with substantially different
decision spaces, as illustrated in
Figure 1 .
Existing work has studied CAD code generation, tool-using agents, execution repair,
and interactive modeling ( Mallis et al. 2024 ; Guan et al. 2025 ; Doris et al. 2025 ; Wang et al. 2025 ; Barkley et al. 2026 ; Gong et al. 2026 ) ,
but the harness itself is typically treated as implementation infrastructure
rather than as a variable that shapes both agent execution and policy learning.
This raises a central question: How should a CAD agent harness represent actions and states so that it
preserves the decisions required for complex modeling while avoiding
representation burden that is irrelevant to the task?

blocks.en:
This trade-off is important in CAD.
A fine-grained coding interface gives the model broad control over the underlying software,
but the same CAD operation can often be expressed through many programs,
command sequences, variable names, temporary objects, and API combinations.
These implementations may produce the same geometric state transition,
but they appear as different generation and supervision targets.
The model must then spend capacity on implementation choices that do not affect the intended state transition.
A semantic interface can remove many of these choices by representing the intended operation directly.
However, excessive compression can hide state differences that require
different actions or remove operations needed for correct modeling and error recovery.
A useful harness must therefore reduce irrelevant representation choices
while preserving the actions and observations needed for correct decisions.

blocks.en:
To make this trade-off explicit, we formalize the model-facing interface as a Harness-Induced CAD Decision Space : a harness maps model outputs to
executable operations, maps internal CAD states to model-visible observations,
and returns execution results as feedback, thereby determining which
operations the agent can perform, which state differences and failures it can
identify, and which policies it can execute and learn. We then introduce the Semantic Decision Bottleneck as a design principle for this space: it
compresses behaviorally equivalent implementations and removes state
information that does not affect the next decision, while preserving the
actions and observations needed to reach the target geometry and recover from
errors.

Following this principle, we develop DeciCAD , a domain-native harness
for closed-loop CAD agents. DeciCAD represents task-relevant design
transitions as semantic CAD actions, grounds these actions in a persistent CAD
document, and returns structured execution feedback together with
decision-oriented observations. We further develop a
harness-grounded learning pipeline that reconstructs causally conditioned
action supervision from successful and recovered interaction trajectories,
initializes CAD action policies through supervised fine-tuning (SFT),
and supports online reinforcement learning (RL) using policy-generated
trajectories and geometry-grounded rewards.

Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD consistently produces more
accurate final geometry than competitive CAD agents and a general-purpose
coding harness, while reducing model-output tokens by 45–88% relative to the
coding harness on text-to-CAD tasks. Observation ablations show that showing more CAD state does not always help: unfiltered state inflates the input context, and coarse feedback strips out what the agent needs in order to recover. With matched training settings, open-weight models trained in the DeciCAD decision space learn stronger long-horizon CAD action policies than the same models trained through code-level interaction.

error recovery, and long-horizon policy learnability significantly.

Our work connects agent interaction interfaces, decision-preserving
abstraction, and policy learning in interactive CAD environments. We review

blocks.en: 2.1 Agent Interfaces and Decision Abstraction
blocks.zh: 2.1 代理接口和决定摘要

blocks.en:

action–state representation that defines the policy space presented to the
model.

representations preserve transition, reward, value, or policy structure ( Ravindran and Barto 2003 ; Li et al. 2006 ; Abel et al. 2016 ; Abel et al. 2020 ) ; the Information Bottleneck similarly retains

semantics. Our Harness-Induced Decision Space describes this transformation,
and the Semantic Decision Bottleneck constrains its compression by decision
preservation.

blocks.zh: 2.2 CAD 一代人和互动代理人

blocks.en:

programs, and interactive actions. DeepCAD and Fusion 360 Gallery represent
structured modeling histories ( Wu et al. 2021 ; Willis et al. 2020 ) ,
while Text2CAD and CADmium learn parametric command sequences from language ( Khan et al. 2024 ; Govindarajan et al. 2026 ) .
CAD-Coder systems generate
executable CAD code ( Guan et al. 2025 ; Doris et al. 2025 ) , and CADFusion,
CADSmith, and CADDesigner incorporate rendering, execution repair, or
multi-agent feedback ( Wang et al. 2025 ; Barkley et al. 2026 ; Fan et al. 2025 ) . Code is
expressive, but also makes program organization and API realization part of
the model output.

blocks.en: 2.3 Policy Learning from Interaction
blocks.zh: 2.3 从互动中学习政策

blocks.en:
Tool policies commonly acquire initial capability from generated or curated
demonstrations ( Schick et al. 2023 ; Li et al. 2023 ; Qin et al. 2024 ) . In a
stateful environment, however, action validity depends on the preceding
trajectory and feedback; imitation therefore encounters distribution shift
when student-induced states depart from teacher trajectories ( Ross et al. 2011 ) . Online methods address this gap using execution
outcomes on states visited by the learned policy ( Feng et al. 2025 ; Qian et al. 2025 ) , including curriculum reinforcement
learning in CAD ( Gong et al. 2026 ) . We align causal supervision,
student rollouts, and environment feedback within the same Harness-Induced
Decision Space, enabling a controlled study of how representation affects both
imitation and online learning.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
The harness determines how the closed CAD loop is presented to the language
model: whether the model writes general-purpose code or selects a semantic CAD
action, which part of the current design is shown, and how execution failures
are reported. We formalize this interaction, formulate the Semantic Decision
Bottleneck, instantiate it in DeciCAD , and use the same
representation for SFT and online RL.

blocks.en:
Action and observation sufficiency specify what a harness must preserve, but
do not uniquely determine its model-facing representation. Among
decision-sufficient interfaces, we prefer those that reduce unnecessary
burden on both model output and input. We refer to this principle as the Semantic Decision Bottleneck : compressing action representations and
visible context while retaining the distinctions required for correct action
selection and error recovery. DeciCAD instantiates this principle
through domain-specific action schemas, concise execution feedback, and
targeted inspection operations that retrieve additional state only when
needed. A formal preference relation over decision-sufficient harnesses is
provided in the appendix.

failure. Action semantics are thus grounded in actual CAD transitions rather

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We formalized Harness-Induced CAD Decision Spaces and instantiated the
Semantic Decision Bottleneck in DeciCAD through semantic actions,
persistent state, and decision-oriented feedback. Across execution, SFT, and
online RL, DeciCAD preserves complex modeling capability while
reducing irrelevant burden and enabling more learnable and optimizable
policies. Together, these findings show that a harness determines both the CAD
operations a model can execute and the distinctions its policy must learn,
while environment feedback improves that policy within the same decision
representation. This establishes harness design as central to CAD agents.
Our study has limitations. The harness comparison uses one CAD backend and
one frontier model, policy learning uses one student model on one dataset,
and mesh-based metrics do not capture editability, constraint satisfaction,
or feature-tree validity. Extending the comparison to further backends,

blocks.en: B.2 Semantic Decision Bottleneck

blocks.en:
Decision sufficiency specifies what a harness must preserve, but does not
uniquely determine how those capabilities are represented to the model. Two
harnesses may connect to the same CAD backend and support the same task-level
operations while exposing different numbers of implementation choices,
different state granularity, and different forms of execution feedback. The
Semantic Decision Bottleneck compares these decision-sufficient
representations, adapting the compression principle of the information
bottleneck to a model-facing action–observation interface ( Tishby et al. 2000 ) .

The main text characterizes a decision-sufficient CAD harness through action

blocks.en: C.1 Semantic CAD Action Space

blocks.en:
A modeling policy first requires an action vocabulary capable of expressing
design intent. DeciCAD represents each model output as a CAD action
with geometric arguments. The vocabulary covers documents and artifacts,
sketches and constraints, solid features, Booleans and patterns, edge
treatments, object placement, assembly, and state inspection. Each action
exposes the variables that determine the CAD state transition. An extrusion,
for example, specifies its profile, material mode, extent, and direction,
while object resolution and CAD API invocation remain within the harness. This
feature-oriented organization follows structured construction histories used
in parametric CAD corpora while exposing them as executable interaction steps ( Wu et al. 2021 ; Willis et al. 2020 ; Khan et al. 2024 ) .

blocks.en: C.2 Grounding Semantic Actions in CAD State
blocks.zh: C.2 在CAD州采取语义行动

blocks.en:
Semantic actions specify what the model can select; state grounding determines
what a selection means in the current design. A point, direction, or rotation
has a unique geometric meaning only relative to an explicit coordinate frame. DeciCAD therefore interprets all action arguments under a shared
spatial contract. Linear quantities use millimeters and angular quantities use
degrees. Documents use a right-handed world frame with (+X) right, (+Y)
back, and (+Z) up, and rotations follow the right-hand rule. Two-dimensional
geometry lies in the right-handed local frame of its sketch, while solid
placement explicitly selects world or parent coordinates. System instructions
state these rules, typed arguments mark the space of each value, and the
execution layer reports authoritative frames read from the actual CAD
placement.

blocks.en:
After an action executes, the model must continue from the resulting
environment state. Expanding the complete CAD document repeatedly introduces
objects and properties irrelevant to the current decision, whereas reporting
only call-level success cannot support geometric judgment or recovery. DeciCAD separates these needs: passive execution feedback describes
the state transition that just occurred, while active hierarchical inspection
retrieves local state needed by the next decision.

generation. A failure response contains an error category, the relevant
argument or object, and a recovery direction. Invalid input, missing
references, geometric failure, conflict, timeout, and unknown outcome remain
distinct because they call for different next actions.

blocks.en:
Across this loop, DeciCAD coordinates compression of model-facing
actions and observations. Semantic actions merge behaviorally equivalent
implementation forms, while the spatial contract, stable references, and
execution verification ensure that the compressed actions still denote
well-defined CAD transitions. Passive feedback omits the complete internal
state, and active inspection restores local distinctions when a decision
requires them. Compression therefore remains constrained by action and
observation sufficiency.

Together, these mechanisms instantiate the Semantic Decision Bottleneck from
the main text. The model generates CAD decisions rather than their expanded
implementations and observes state evidence supporting the next decision
rather than the full internal representation of the CAD system. Coordinating
actions, grounding, and observations in the same closed loop reduces
representation burden without removing the decision paths required for task
completion and error recovery.

In the concrete code organization, these mechanisms are separated into three
connected components. The harness runtime organizes the decision loop across
model invocation, action execution, and feedback. An interface-contract layer
defines semantic actions, geometric representations, and execution results.
A backend execution layer binds those contracts to native operations in a
specific CAD system. This organization allows the interaction policy, the
model-visible interface, and CAD execution logic to evolve independently. A
new CAD backend implements the same action and feedback contracts while
preserving the model-facing decision space.

blocks.en:
DeciCAD is distributed as a terminal-native Agentic CAD application.
It organizes model providers, specialized agents, CAD backends, and project
resources in one workspace, allowing a user to create, modify, inspect,
assemble, and export native CAD documents through natural-language
interaction. This section presents the resulting product workflow, its support
for long-horizon multi-agent projects, the backend SDK available to developers,
and our official FreeCAD integration. Its streamed action–observation loop
follows the interaction pattern established by language agents while grounding

blocks.en: E.2 Control Plane for Multi-Agent CAD Work
blocks.zh: E.2 多代理CAD控制计划 工作

blocks.en:
The interactive loop is supported by an application-level control plane that
coordinates agents, tools, resources, permissions, and persistent project
state. CAD backends execute domain operations, but they do not decide which
agent may act, which calls may run concurrently, or whether an action was based
on a current document revision. Keeping these responsibilities in the control
plane allows the same orchestration policy to operate across compatible CAD
systems.
blocks.zh:
交互循环由应用程序级控制平面支持,该平面
协调代理、工具、资源、权限和持久项目
状态。 CAD 后端执行域操作,但他们不决定哪个
代理人可以采取行动,而这种呼吁可以同时进行,或者一项行动是否基于
关于当前文件的修订。 将这些责任置于控制之下
平面允许相同的管弦政策在兼容的 CAD 中运行
系统。

blocks.en:
For larger projects, a leader agent retains the user conversation and overall
goal while delegating bounded subtasks to four built-in roles. The Designer
turns functional and geometric intent into a feature and interface plan; the
Modeler owns one complete part or a dependency-ordered modeling stage; the
Assembler inserts components and manages placements, grounding, mates, and
solve state; and the Verifier performs an independent, predominantly read-only
evidence pass over the final document and exported assets. Each child receives
the original request together with a bounded assignment, separate context,
role-specific instructions, tool allowlist, and interaction budget. A child
cannot recursively create more agents or modify the leader’s task board. Its
final response is returned as evidence together with the resources changed
during execution, leaving acceptance and follow-up decisions with the leader.
blocks.zh:
对于较大的项目,一个领导代理保留了用户谈话和总体
目标,同时将捆绑的子任务委托给四个内置角色. 设计师
将功能和几何意图转化为特性和接口计划;
建模师拥有一个完整的部分或一个依赖性订购的建模阶段;
Assembler 插入组件并管理放置、搁浅、配对和
解析状态; 验证器执行独立且主要只读状态
证据通过最后文件和出口资产。 每个儿童得到
原始请求连同有限度的转让,单独上下文,
特定角色指令、工具授权列表和互动预算。 一个孩子
无法连续创建更多代理或修改领导者的任务委员会。 内容
最后答复连同资源变动作为证据退回

blocks.en:
Multi-stage work is represented by a compact project task graph. Tasks record
their status, description, dependencies, blocking relations, and completion
evidence. This graph separates conversational planning from execution state:
the leader can recover which components are ready, which assembly step is
blocked, and which verification remains after context compaction or session
resumption. Dependency updates are serialized by the control plane, preventing
two agents from concurrently producing inconsistent task-board transitions.
blocks.zh:

其地位、描述、依赖、阻碍关系和完成
证据。 此图将对话计划与执行状态区分开来:

blocks.en:
Every tool specification declares static resource behavior, including the
arguments that identify reads, writes, observations, creations, or filesystem
materialization. Before execution, the resource manager resolves those fields
to concrete document, entity, topology, assembly, or file keys. Each agent also
maintains the revisions it has actually observed. A write is authorized only
when its dependent resources have been observed at their current revisions;
if another agent has modified one of them, the stale write is rejected with a
recoverable conflict and the agent must inspect the updated state. File edits
follow the same rule and require a complete prior read. This observation-based
authorization prevents a plausible but outdated model context from silently
overwriting newer CAD or project state.
blocks.zh:
每个工具规格都声明静态资源行为,包括
用于识别读、写、观察、创建或文件系统的参数
实现。 执行前, 资源管理器会解决这些字段
到具体文档、实体、地形、组装或文件键。 每个代理也

(a) 其依赖的资源在目前的修订中已观察到;

可恢复冲突,代理商必须检查更新状态. 文件编辑

blocks.en:
Independent child assignments can be emitted together and run concurrently.
Tool specifications additionally assign calls to execution lanes and mark them
as parallel or exclusive. After resource resolution, write scopes are sorted
and locked in a deterministic order; calls with disjoint scopes proceed in
parallel, while overlapping CAD writes are serialized. Authorization is
revalidated immediately before execution to close the interval between
scheduling and dispatch. A successful backend result reports concrete RuntimeResourceEffects ; the control plane commits these effects,
advances resource generations, records the responsible agent, and invalidates
stale observations held elsewhere. A failed call does not claim a state
transition. If transport fails after a potentially mutating call, the affected
scope is conservatively invalidated so that later decisions re-inspect it.

blocks.en:
This protocol supports useful concurrency without treating the CAD document as
an ordinary shared text buffer. Different Modelers may construct independent
parts simultaneously, after which an Assembler consumes their committed
outputs. Calls that touch the same body, assembly, or output file are ordered,
and each downstream agent receives only the document revisions known to be
valid at delegation time.

Workspace trust and permission checks are evaluated before protected files or
CAD resources are exposed to an agent. The user remains the authority for
access that crosses the active project boundary or carries elevated effects.
Because permissions are evaluated in the application rather than reimplemented
by every backend, adding a CAD integration does not create a second,
backend-specific authorization path.

blocks.en:
The control plane projects model messages, tool calls, execution outcomes,
permissions, resource commits, task changes, and compaction events onto an
append-only rollout. The same event stream drives the terminal interface and
provides the state required for replay and session restoration. /resume reconstructs an earlier project session, while /compact replaces older interaction with a bounded summary and keeps
recent decisions available to the model. Durable memory is extracted from
completed root rollouts with links to its source turns, separating persistent
design facts from transient dialogue. Skills add reusable CAD procedures,
hooks connect project workflows to agent and tool lifecycle events, and a
project-level AGENTS.md carries coordinate conventions, naming rules,
and delivery requirements into subsequent sessions. Together, these services
allow long-running CAD work to remain recoverable, inspectable, and governed by
one consistent project state.

blocks.en: E.3 Adapting a CAD Backend with the DeciCAD SDK
blocks.zh: E.3 用DeciCAD SDK调整 CAD 后端

blocks.en:
The DeciCAD SDK is the contract boundary shared by the application and backend
implementations. It defines canonical tool names, typed input and output
models, geometry types, opaque object references, permission requirements,
runtime resource effects, structured success values, and model-facing errors.
The application remains responsible for model interaction, agent orchestration,
permissions, sessions, and resource coordination. A backend developer maps the
canonical state transitions to the native API of a target CAD system.
blocks.zh:
十二国联盟 SDK 是应用程序和后端共享的合同边界
执行。 它定义了词汇工具名称、输入和输出
模型,几何类型,不透明的对象引用,权限要求,
运行时资源效应、结构化成功值和模型化错误。
该应用仍然负责模型交互,代理管弦,
权限、会话和资源协调。 后端开发者映射
canonical状态向目标CAD系统的原生API过渡.

blocks.en:
This separation makes the SDK a semantic contract rather than a convenience
wrapper around one vendor API. Canonical tools are grouped into document,
inspection, entity, sketch, solid, and assembly domains. Their Pydantic models
normalize units, frames, geometric values, operation modes, and result shapes,
while DocumentRef and EntityRef preserve backend-owned object
identity as opaque values. A backend imports these specifications instead of
copying or redefining them. Consequently, field descriptions, model-facing tool
schemas, resource declarations, and output validation remain identical across
integrations, while implementation instructions can still describe behavior
specific to the target CAD application.
blocks.zh:
这种分离使得SDK成为语义合同而非方便
包在一个销售商API。 分类工具分为文件、
检查、实体、草图、固体和组装域。 他们的Pydantic模型
常规单位、框架、几何值、操作模式和结果形状,
文档参考和实体参考保存后端拥有的对象
作为不透明值的身份。 后端导入这些规格而不是
复制或重新界定。 因此,实地说明、模型制作工具
整个计划、资源申报和产出验证保持不变
集成,而执行指令仍然可以描述行为
具体针对目标CAD应用.

blocks.en:
A backend first imports a canonical ToolSpec and binds it to an async
implementation with @tool . Inputs have already passed the spec’s
Pydantic validation before execution. The implementation returns the canonical
output model together with accurate RuntimeResourceEffects ; these
effects let the application update resource versions, permissions, and locks.
Recoverable CAD failures use a compact ToolError , keeping operational
failures distinct from backend defects and transport errors. The following
example summarizes the binding used for native document creation.

The server reserves standard output for newline-delimited JSON-RPC frames and
sends operational diagnostics to standard error, keeping transport parseable

is missing, a tool name is duplicated, an imported spec differs from the SDK,
or the manifest targets incompatible SDK, protocol, or tool-contract versions.
Successful results are validated against the exact output model before they
cross the process boundary; operational failure results contain a ToolError and cannot claim resource effects.

blocks.en:
These constraints reduce the work required from a backend developer. The SDK
provides model schemas, validation, RPC framing, process lifecycle, contract
negotiation, error serialization, and the client-side Tool bindings.
The developer concentrates on object resolution, native CAD calls, readiness,
and accurate resource effects. A real BackendClient / BackendServer initialization test exercises the same registry and
wire contract used by the product, catching integration drift before an agent
can invoke the backend. The application and backend may then be released
independently whenever their declared contracts remain compatible; an
incompatible release fails explicitly at activation instead of producing
ambiguous behavior midway through a modeling task.

blocks.en: E.4 FreeCAD as the Reference Backend

blocks.en:
Our official reference backend instantiates this SDK boundary for FreeCAD,
and all experiments in this paper use this backend. The
backend manager shown in Figure 14 controls its
installation, activation, health checking, update, and removal through an
isolated managed environment. In development mode, the setup command also
installs a FreeCAD Addon into the versioned user directory discovered from the
actual FreeCAD runtime, supporting system, portable, and custom installations.

安装、激活、健康检查、更新和清除

blocks.en:
The integration uses two local communication layers. The SDK BackendClient communicates with an independent backend process; that
process connects through an authenticated loopback bridge to FreeCAD’s
embedded Python runtime. The bridge executes CAD operations on the FreeCAD GUI
thread, wraps document writes in native transactions, and encodes the result
under the canonical output model. The bridge panel exposes connection state,
dynamic endpoint, protocol version, age of the last authenticated request, and
start, stop, restart, and automatic-start controls, while the application sees
only the stable SDK contract. Keeping the bridge protocol separate is necessary
because FreeCAD owns the embedded interpreter and GUI event loop; it also keeps
FreeCAD object lookup, argument decoding, result encoding, transaction handling,
and native diagnostics out of the application process.

动态端点、 协议版本、 上次认证请求的年代以及
启动、停止、重新启动和自动启动控制,而应用程序则看到
只有稳定的SDK合同。 有必要将桥梁协议分开
因为 FreeCAD 拥有嵌入式解释器和 GUI 事件环路; 它也保存着
FreeCAD 对象查询,参数解码,结果编码,交易处理,
以及申请过程中的本地诊断。

Table 8 summarizes the complete canonical operation
set currently implemented by the reference backend. Stable opaque references
connect documents, entities, geometry, topology, features, and assembly objects
across calls. Successful tools report concrete resource effects, and failures
are mapped into shared error categories, so the general agent and resource
runtime do not depend on the FreeCAD Python API.

blocks.en:
Inspection is hierarchical rather than a full document dump. Paginated list
operations expose document structure and stable references, after which get
operations retrieve detailed properties, placement, geometry, topology, or
assembly state only for selected objects. Modeling tools return compact native
results and resource effects immediately after execution. This supports the
same active and passive observation pattern used by the DeciCAD decision loop
while retaining direct access to FreeCAD’s editable feature history.
blocks.zh:
检查是分级的,而不是一个完整的文件堆。 已标注列表
操作显示文档结构和稳定的引用,然后得到
操作获取详细属性、位置、几何、地形或
只为选定的对象装配状态。 模拟工具返回本地
执行后立即产生结果和资源影响。 这支持
DeciCAD 决策循环所使用的相同主动和被动观测模式
,同时保留直接访问 FreeCAD 的可编辑特性历史 。

blocks.en:
For batch evaluation and data collection, multiple workers run isolated
FreeCAD and backend processes with separate bridge endpoints, authentication
tokens, instance identifiers, and result caches. A worker resets and verifies
all open documents before accepting another episode. This isolation prevents
CAD state from leaking across tasks while retaining the same backend contract
used by the interactive product.
blocks.zh:
就批量评估和数据收集而言,多个工人进行隔离
FreeCAD 和具有单独桥端、认证的后端进程
符号、实例标识符和结果缓存。 工人转业核实
所有打开的文档,然后接受另一集。 这种隔离可以防止
CAD 状态来自跨任务泄露,同时保留相同的后端合同
用于交互式产品。

blocks.en:
Parallelism is therefore process-isolated rather than implemented by issuing
concurrent CAD operations inside one FreeCAD instance. Each worker owns one
FreeCAD process, one Addon bridge, and one matching backend process. Distinct
endpoint descriptor files lead to independent dynamic loopback ports and
authentication tokens. This design supports parallel interactive services,
trajectory collection, and benchmark evaluation without sharing mutable
FreeCAD state across tasks.
blocks.zh:
因此,并行性是程序孤立的,而不是通过发行来实现。
在一个 FreeCAD 实例中同时进行 CAD 操作 。 每个工人都有一个
FreeCAD进程,一个Addon桥,和一个匹配的后端进程. 区分
端点描述文件导致独立的动态回路端口和
认证符. 此设计支持平行交互服务,
轨迹收集和基准评价,不分享可变
FreeCAD状态跨越任务.
